Prerequisite: The FortiADC registered with Fortinet Customer Service and Support, with a valid Fortinet Technical Support (FortiCare) contract, and each purchased FortiGuard service license or license bundle registered to it
What it enables: Service from the FortiGuard Distribution Network (FDN), which validates the licenses P3 to P7 and sends updates only to a FortiADC with a valid license, and the firmware downloads from the support site
How to put it in place: Register on the support site, upload the license in GUI: System > FortiGuard (Upgrade License), and check the support contract and each service in GUI: System > FortiGuard (Support Contract and FortiGuard Services) and the Licenses widget in GUI: Dashboard > Main
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Step 5: Complete product registration, licensing, and upgrades" (registration is required to download firmware), "Connecting to FortiGuard services" (you must first register the FortiADC and have a valid support contract that includes service subscriptions), and "Configuring FortiGuard service settings" (if the license is invalid, FortiGuard does not send updates)

Prerequisite: A path from the FortiADC to the FDN: correct time and time zone, DNS servers that resolve update.fortiguard.net, routes, and NAT and firewall devices that allow the FortiGuard ports; or an override FortiGuard server (for example the built-in FDS of a FortiManager in a closed network) or an explicit web proxy
What it enables: License validation and updates of the WAF signature, IP reputation, Geo IP, IPS, antivirus, and DLP databases (P3 to P7), and automatic patch upgrades from FortiGuard
How to put it in place: Check with execute ping <FORTIGUARD_FQDN> and execute traceroute <FORTIGUARD_FQDN>; override server: config system fortiguard; set override-server-status enable; set override-server-address <FDS_ADDRESS>; end; web proxy: config system fortiguard; set tunneling-status enable; set tunneling-address <PROXY_ADDRESS>; set tunneling-port <PROXY_PORT>; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Connecting to FortiGuard services" (the settings to verify, License validation with FortiManager, and Accessing FortiGuard via a proxy) and "Validating a VM license with no internet connection"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard WAF Signature license, or a license bundle that includes Web Application Security Signatures (the Application Security or AI Security bundle)
What it enables: Web attack signature database updates, the Known Good Bot and Malicious Bot signatures and lists that bot detection uses, WAF signature staging, and WAF adaptive learning
How to put it in place: Purchase the license, register it (P1), and check WAF Signature in GUI: System > FortiGuard (FortiGuard Services)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring FortiGuard service settings" (WAF Signature service), "Licensing requirements" (WAF adaptive learning needs the WAF Signature license or Application Security bundle license), and "Bot Detection" (Before you begin: WAF Signature Database updates, including bot signatures); FortiADC 7.4.2 Release Notes, "What's new" (New FortiADC License Bundles)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard IP Reputation and Geo IP service license, or a license bundle that includes it (the Network Security, Application Security, or AI Security bundle)
What it enables: The IP reputation database (including its Internet Service Database entries) and the Geo IP database that IP reputation and Geo IP block lists and allowlists check client addresses against
How to put it in place: Purchase the license, register it (P1), and check IP Reputation and Geo IP in GUI: System > FortiGuard (FortiGuard Services)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Connecting to FortiGuard services" (license status for services like WAF and IP Reputation; the FDN updates the IP Reputation and Geo IP databases) and "Configuring FortiGuard service settings"; FortiADC 7.4.2 Release Notes, "What's new" (the Network Security Bundle includes IP Reputation and GeoIP)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard AntiVirus license, or a license bundle that includes it (the Network Security, Application Security, or AI Security bundle)
What it enables: Antivirus database and engine updates for antivirus scanning, including delta packages
How to put it in place: Purchase the license, register it (P1), and check Antivirus in GUI: System > FortiGuard (FortiGuard Services)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring FortiGuard service settings" (Antivirus service) and "AntiVirus" (signatures are updated from FortiGuard); FortiADC 7.4.2 Release Notes, "What's new" (the Network Security Bundle includes FortiGuard AntiVirus)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Intrusion Prevention license, or a license bundle that includes it (the Network Security, Application Security, or AI Security bundle)
What it enables: Regular and extended IPS database and IPS engine updates for IPS profiles
How to put it in place: Purchase the license, register it (P1), and check Intrusion Prevention in GUI: System > FortiGuard (FortiGuard Services)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring FortiGuard service settings" (Intrusion Prevention service); FortiADC 7.4.2 Release Notes, "What's new" (the Network Security Bundle includes Intrusion Prevention)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard DLP service license, separate or in a bundle that includes it (the Application Security or AI Security bundle)
What it enables: The predefined FortiGuard DLP data types, dictionaries, and sensors used by data loss prevention policies
How to put it in place: Purchase the license, register it (P1), and check Data Loss Prevention in GUI: System > FortiGuard (FortiGuard Services)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "FortiGuard DLP service" (FortiGuard DLP service license; you must have a valid license and have enabled the service); FortiADC 7.4.2 Release Notes, "What's new" (the Application Security Bundle includes FortiGuard DLP)

Prerequisite: The back-end application servers, defined as real servers and reachable from FortiADC
What it enables: Real server pools and their health checks, and real server SSL profiles, which a pool uses
How to put it in place: config load-balance real-server; edit <REAL_SERVER>; set ip <SERVER_IP>; set status enable; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring real servers" and "Using Real server pools"

Prerequisite: A virtual server that receives the application traffic and uses the profile or policy (a Layer 7 virtual server for the WAF, user authentication, and most security profiles)
What it enables: Every profile, policy, and list setting in the map, which takes effect only on the traffic of a virtual server that uses it
How to put it in place: config load-balance virtual-server; edit <VS>; set type l7-load-balance; set load-balance-profile <LB_PROFILE>; set load-balance-pool <POOL>; set waf-profile <WAF_PROFILE>; set status enable; next; end (name the profile the row sets)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Advanced Mode: Configuring a Layer 7 Virtual Server"; chapter row "Virtual servers (Layer 2, Layer 4, and Layer 7)"

Prerequisite: The DoD root and intermediate CA certificates imported into the FortiADC trust store, and grouped in a CA group where a setting names one
What it enables: Certificate verification of clients, real servers, GSLB peers, and LDAPS servers against the DoD PKI
How to put it in place: Import them in GUI: System > Certificates; config system certificate ca_group; edit <CA_GROUP>; config group_member; edit 1; set ca <DOD_CA>; next; end; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Certificates" and "Validating certificates"; chapter row "Local, CA, and intermediate CA certificates (trust store)"

Prerequisite: DoD OCSP responders and CRL distribution points reachable from FortiADC
What it enables: Revocation checks in certificate verification (OCSP and CRL)
How to put it in place: Allow FortiADC to reach the responder and CRL URLs; check with execute ping <OCSP_OR_CRL_HOST>
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Validating certificates"; chapter rows "Certificate verification (CA group, OCSP, and CRL)" and "Certificate revocation lists (CRL)"

Prerequisite: A server certificate issued to the FortiADC by the DoD PKI, imported as a local certificate with its intermediate CAs, and placed in a local certificate group for a client SSL profile
What it enables: TLS on the web UI, SSL offloading on virtual servers, the SAML service provider signing certificate, and GSLB peer authentication with a DoD-issued certificate
How to put it in place: Import it in GUI: System > Certificates; config system certificate local_cert_group; edit <CERT_GROUP>; config group_member; edit 1; set local-cert <DOD_ISSUED_CERT>; set intermediate-ca-group <INTERMEDIATE_CA_GROUP>; next; end; next; end; config load-balance client-ssl-profile; edit <CLIENT_SSL_PROFILE>; set local-certificate-group <CERT_GROUP>; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Importing a local certificate", "Creating a local certificate group", "Configuring Client SSL profiles", and "Certificate guidelines" (for SSL offloading, a local certificate group references the server certificate and its intermediate CA group)

Prerequisite: A subordinate CA certificate and private key for re-signing, issued by the DoD PKI or the organization's PKI, imported on the FortiADC and trusted by the clients
What it enables: SSL forward proxy (SSL inspection), which re-signs server certificates
How to put it in place: Import it in GUI: System > Certificates (then distribute the CA certificate to the clients)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Certificate guidelines" (for SSL decryption by forward proxy, a local certificate group and an intermediate CA group with the CA and key; a browser trusts the certificate only if the CA is installed in it) and "SSL decryption by forward proxy"

Prerequisite: A certificate verify object that lists the DoD CA certificates (P10) and, where required, the OCSP and CRL objects
What it enables: Client certificate authentication (mutual TLS), real server certificate verification, and advanced mutual TLS options
How to put it in place: config system certificate certificate_verify; edit <VERIFY>; config group_member; edit 1; set ca-certificate <DOD_CA>; next; end; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Validating certificates"; chapter row "Certificate verification (CA group, OCSP, and CRL)"

Prerequisite: A SafeNet Network HSM (the only HSM FortiADC supports; FIPS-validated where FIPS is required) with a partition for FortiADC, the FortiADC registered as its client, and HSM support enabled on the FortiADC
What it enables: Keeping the private keys of virtual server certificates in the HSM
How to put it in place: Prepare the HSM partition and client registration on the HSM, then configure the HSM on the FortiADC (HSM support is enabled with set hsm enable under config system global, an option the 8.0.3 CLI Reference does not list)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "HSM Integration" (Integrating FortiADC with SafeNet Network HSM; FortiADC supports the SafeNet Network HSM only)

Prerequisite: A hardware model with a Trusted Platform Module: 220F, 320F, 420F, 1200F, 2200F, or 4200F
What it enables: Hardware-backed storage of the private data encryption key; on other systems the key is kept in a file on the system
How to put it in place: Model selection; check the model in GUI: System > FortiGuard (Support Contract: Hardware)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 CLI Reference, "config system global" (private-data-encryption: TPM-based encrypted key storage is available on the listed hardware models)

Prerequisite: The other members of the HA cluster: the same hardware model running the identical firmware version, each with a valid license (a paid license for FortiADC-VM; trial licenses are not supported) and registered with its FortiGuard services, and physical ports for heartbeat and data traffic (a crossover cable for active-passive, a shared Layer 2 switch for active-active)
What it enables: High availability clusters and the HA management interface
How to put it in place: Install and license the peers, cable the heartbeat and data ports, and configure HA on each node with config system ha; set mode active-passive; set group-id <GROUP_ID>; set hbdev <HB_PORT>; set datadev <DATA_PORT>; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "High Availability" (HA system requirements) and the deployment steps for each HA mode (license and register all FortiADC appliances in the cluster)

Prerequisite: An access profile that grants the administrator only the permissions the role needs
What it enables: Local, remote, and SSO administrator accounts, and the access profile override from RADIUS or TACACS+, which applies only profiles defined on the FortiADC
How to put it in place: config system accprofile; edit <PROFILE>; set system read; set log read; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring access profiles"; FortiADC 8.0.3 CLI Reference, "config system admin" (accprofile-override)

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server that authenticates the administrators (enforcing DoD PKI or MFA) and, for the overrides, returns the access profile or VDOM in the Fortinet vendor-specific attribute
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication with RADIUS and the access profile and VDOM overrides
How to put it in place: Set up the server and its shared secret, then config user radius; edit <RADIUS>; set server <RADIUS_SERVER>; set secret <SECRET>; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Remote Server"; FortiADC 8.0.3 CLI Reference, "config system admin" (accprofile-override and vdom-override)

Prerequisite: An LDAP directory server reachable over LDAPS or StartTLS, with an account and base DN for FortiADC
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication with LDAP
How to put it in place: config user ldap; edit <LDAP>; set server <LDAP_SERVER>; set port 636; set cnid <CNID>; set dn <BASE_DN>; next; end; LDAPS or StartTLS and the CA are set in GUI: Application Access Manager > Remote Server
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Remote Server"; chapter row "Remote administrator authentication with LDAP"

Prerequisite: A TACACS+ server that authenticates the administrators and, for the overrides, returns the access profile (admin_prof) or VDOM
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication with TACACS+ and the access profile and VDOM overrides
How to put it in place: config user tacacs+; edit <TACACS>; set server <TACACS_SERVER>; set secret <SECRET>; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Remote Server"; FortiADC 8.0.3 CLI Reference, "config system admin" (accprofile-override and vdom-override)

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider that authenticates the users (with DoD PKI where required), and its metadata file imported on the FortiADC
What it enables: SAML single sign-on for the users of a virtual server
How to put it in place: Import the IdP metadata in GUI: Application Access Manager > SAML
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "SAML" (To import a SAML IDP metadata file)

Prerequisite: A root FortiGate that acts as the SAML identity provider of the Security Fabric, with the FortiADC joined to the Fabric and authorized on the FortiGate, and Configuration Sync set to retrieve the IdP metadata
What it enables: Administrator single sign-on through the FortiGate Security Fabric
How to put it in place: config system csf; set status enable; set upstream-ip <FORTIGATE_IP>; set configuration-sync default; set management-ip <MGMT_IP>; end, then authorize the FortiADC on the FortiGate
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 CLI Reference, "config system sso-admin" (Before you begin: the Fabric connector configured and authorized, Configuration Sync enabled) and "config system csf"; FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "FortiGate Security Fabric Connector"

Prerequisite: The application users and the server that holds them: local users, or an LDAP, RADIUS, or TACACS+ server, as members of a user group
What it enables: User authentication policies, authentication session settings, and unified access policies that name the user group
How to put it in place: config user user-group; edit <USER_GROUP>; config member; edit 1; set type ldap; set ldap-server <LDAP>; next; end; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "User Group", "Local User", and "Remote Server"

Prerequisite: An authentication policy that names the user group (P24)
What it enables: User authentication on a virtual server and the AAG portal
How to put it in place: config load-balance auth-policy; edit <AUTH_POLICY>; set user-group <USER_GROUP>; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "User Authentication"; chapter row "Unified access policy for application access control"

Prerequisite: FortiClient EMS 7.0.3 or later with the FortiADC authorized as a Fabric device, endpoints running FortiClient 7.0.1 or later, and a FortiADC platform that supports FortiClient EMS (the listed hardware models, BYOL cloud instances, or the listed VM environments; a VM needs a certificate-embedded license); then a ZTNA profile
What it enables: Zero Trust Network Access on Layer 7 HTTPS and TCPS virtual servers
How to put it in place: Configure the connector in GUI: Security Fabric > Fabric Connectors (FortiClient EMS) and authorize the FortiADC in EMS; create the ZTNA profile in GUI: Network Security > ZTNA
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "FortiClient EMS Connector" (Requirements), "Configuring FortiClient EMS Connector for ZTNA", and "Configuring a ZTNA Profile" (Before you begin)

Prerequisite: An on-premises FortiSandbox appliance reachable from the FortiADC (in HA mode, with the default source IP)
What it enables: Submission of files from antivirus scanning to FortiSandbox
How to put it in place: Configure the connector in GUI: Security Fabric > Fabric Connectors (FortiSandbox, Type FSA)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "FortiSandbox Connector" and "AntiVirus" (Important Notes)

Prerequisite: An external ICAP server reachable from the FortiADC, with the service name (reqmod or respmod) that the server expects
What it enables: Offloading file inspection from antivirus profiles (HTTP and HTTPS traffic)
How to put it in place: Configure the connector in GUI: Security Fabric > Fabric Connectors (ICAP Server)
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "ICAP Server Connector"

Prerequisite: Remote syslog servers (or a SIEM) that accept TCP over TLS
What it enables: Off-loading of event, security, and traffic logs
How to put it in place: Set up the server, then config log setting remote; edit <SYSLOG_ID>; set status enable; set server <SYSLOG_SERVER>; set proto tcpssl; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring syslog settings"

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer reachable from the FortiADC that accepts its logs
What it enables: Log transport to FortiAnalyzer over OFTP
How to put it in place: Allow the FortiADC on the FortiAnalyzer, then config log setting fortianalyzer; set status enable; set server <FAZ_SERVER>; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring OFTP settings for FortiAnalyzer logs" and "FortiAnalyzer Connector"

Prerequisite: An SMTP server that relays alert email over STARTTLS, and the addresses of the ISSO and administrators who receive it
What it enables: Alert email and email automation actions
How to put it in place: config system mailserver; set address <SMTP_SERVER>; set security starttls; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring an SMTP mail server"

Prerequisite: Authoritative NTP servers (DoD or organization time sources), with the shared key and key ID where NTP authentication is used
What it enables: Time synchronization and NTP authentication
How to put it in place: Set up the servers and keys, then config system time ntp; set ntpsync enable; config ntp-server; edit 1; set server <NTP_SERVER>; next; end; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring system time"

Prerequisite: An SNMP manager configured with the same SNMPv3 user, authentication protocol, and privacy protocol
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and traps
How to put it in place: Configure the matching user on the SNMP manager
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Configuring SNMP v3"

Prerequisite: An SFTP server with an account and folder for the FortiADC backups
What it enables: Scheduled configuration backups
How to put it in place: Set up the server, then config system auto-backup; set storage sftp; set address <SFTP_SERVER>; set username <USER>; set password <PASSWORD>; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 CLI Reference, "config system auto-backup"; chapter row "Scheduled configuration backup"

Prerequisite: A FortiADC Manager that manages the FortiADC
What it enables: Central management of the configuration
How to put it in place: config system central-management; set status enable; set mgmt-type FortiADC-Manager; set mgmt-addr <MANAGER_ADDRESS>; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "FortiADC Manager Connector"

Prerequisite: An HTTP or HTTPS server that publishes the IP list as a plain text file (up to 1 MB), and an IP Address connector that imports it
What it enables: External IP lists as the source or destination of firewall policy rules
How to put it in place: config system external-resource; edit <EXTERNAL_LIST>; set type address; set resource <LIST_URL>; set status enable; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "IP Address Connector" (Requirements)

Prerequisite: Virtual domains enabled and the VDOMs created
What it enables: VDOM administrators and the VDOM override, which requires VDOM mode
How to put it in place: config system global; set vdom-admin enable; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Virtual Domain (VDOM) and Administrative Domain (ADOM) overview"; FortiADC 8.0.3 CLI Reference, "config system admin" (vdom-override requires VDOM mode)

Prerequisite: At least one other administrator account with global access that has been tested, so the built-in admin account can be disabled
What it enables: Disabling the default admin account
How to put it in place: config system admin; edit <ADMIN>; set is-system-admin yes; set access-profile <PROFILE>; next; end
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 CLI Reference, "config system global" (default-admin) and "config system admin" (is-system-admin); chapter row "Disable the default admin account"

Prerequisite: FortiIdentity Cloud, with the FortiADC registered on the same account as the FortiIdentity Cloud contracts, and a FortiADC that is not in HA (FortiIdentity Cloud is not supported in HA)
What it enables: Two-factor authentication for local administrators
How to put it in place: Set Two-factor Authentication to FortiIdentity Cloud for the administrator in GUI: System > Administrator
Source: FortiADC 8.0.3 Administration Guide, "Creating administrator users" (Two-factor Authentication; not supported in HA condition) and "Local User" (the device must be registered on the same account as the FortiIdentity Cloud contracts)
